He also narrated it from Musaddad, from Mu'tamir, with the same chain. Then he narrated it from Musaddad, from Yazid ibn Zurai', from al-Taymi, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi', and mentioned it [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (768)]. Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also related it through several routes from Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi, with the same chain [Sahih Muslim, no. (578); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1408); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/161)]. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Allah, the Exalted, says: "When the sky splits open" — and that is the Day of Resurrection — "and it hearkens to its Lord" — i.e., it listens to its Lord and obeys His command concerning what He commanded it, of splitting — "and it has the right to do so" — i.e., it is right for it to obey His command, because He is the Mighty, who cannot be prevented or overcome, rather He has subdued everything, and everything is humbled before Him.

Then He said: "And when the earth is stretched out" — i.e., spread out, laid flat, and expanded.

I will be the first to be called, and Jibril will be on the right of the Most Merciful; I had never seen him before. I will say: O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: He has spoken the truth. Then I will intercede, and I will say: O Lord, Your servants have worshipped You at the ends of the earth." His saying: "And it casts out what is in it and empties itself" — i.e., it casts out what is in its belly of the dead, and empties itself of them. This was said by Mujahid, Sa'id and Qatadah. "And it hearkens to its Lord and has the right to do so," as has preceded.

* *

His saying: "O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet it" — i.e., you are striving toward your Lord with striving, and working a work, "and you will meet it" — then indeed you will meet what you did of good or evil. What supports this is what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said: O Muhammad, live as you wish, for you will die; and love whom you wish, for you will part from him; and do what you wish, for you will meet it" [Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (1755)].

Some people return the pronoun to His saying "your Lord" — i.e., "you will meet your Lord" — and its meaning is that He will recompense you for your deed and reward you for your striving. According to this, both opinions are mutually consistent.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor" — he says: you work a work by which you will meet Allah, good or evil.

Qatadah said: "O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor" — indeed your labor, O son of Adam, is weak; so whoever is able to make his labor in obedience to Allah, let him do it, and there is no power except with Allah.

Then He said: "As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a light account" — i.e., an easy reckoning without difficulty, meaning that every detail of his deeds will not be scrutinized; for whoever is reckoned in that manner will certainly perish.

Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Hamzah ibn ['In M: "from".] 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say in some of his prayer: "O Allah, reckon with me with an easy reckoning." (1755)].

Some people return the pronoun to His saying "your Lord" — i.e., "you will meet your Lord" — and its meaning is that He will recompense you for your deed and reward you for your striving. According to this, both opinions are mutually consistent.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor" — he says: you work a work by which you will meet Allah, good or evil.

Qatadah said: "O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor" — indeed your labor, O son of Adam, is weak; so whoever is able to make his labor in obedience to Allah, let him do it, and there is no power except with Allah.

I said: "Does not Allah say: 'He will be called to a light account'?" He said: "That is the presentation; indeed, whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning is punished," and he moved his hand over his finger as if he were tapping.

(4939); Sahih Muslim, no. (2876)].

When he finished, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the easy reckoning?" He said: "That he looks into his record and is pardoned for it. Indeed, whoever is scrutinized in the reckoning, O 'A'ishah, on that day perishes." Sound according to the conditions of Muslim [al-Musnad (6/48)].

"Indeed, he thought he would never return" — i.e., he believed that he would not return to Allah and would not be brought back after his death. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and others. Al-Hawr means return. Allah said: "Yes! Indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him" — meaning: Yes, Allah will indeed bring him back as He originated him, and will recompense him for his deeds, good and bad, for He "was ever Seeing of him" — i.e., Knowing and Aware.

"Gathered together, if only they found a driver..."

Ikrimah said: ﴿wa al-layli wa ma wasaq﴾ means: what it drives of darkness; when night comes, every thing goes to its shelter.

* *

* *

I say: they mean the night of the Isra'.

Al-Suddi himself said: ﴿latarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: the deeds of those before you, station after station.

I say: it seems he intended the meaning of the authentic hadith: "You will surely follow the ways of those before you, step by step, so exactly that if they entered a lizard's hole, you would enter it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" [The hadith's takhrij was mentioned in the commentary on verse 34 of Surat al-Tawbah.] This is possible.

Al-A'mash said: Ibrahim related to me, he said: Abdullah said: ﴿latarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: "The sky splits, then turns red, then becomes one color after another."

Al-Thawri related from Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: "The sky is sometimes like oil-dregs (al-dihan), and sometimes it splits."

Al-Bazzar related through the chain of Jabir al-Ju'fi, from al-Sha'bi, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿latarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾, "O Muhammad", meaning state after state. Then he said: Jabir also related it from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿latarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: "People who were lowly in their affairs in the world, who will be elevated in the Hereafter, and others who were noble in the world, who will be humbled in the Hereafter."

Ikrimah said: ﴿tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: state after state, weaning after having been a suckling infant, and old age after having been youth.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: state after state, ease after hardship, hardship after ease, wealth after poverty, poverty after wealth, health after sickness, and sickness after health.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Abdullah ibn Zahir: my father related to me, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir (al-Ju'fi), from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed the son of Adam is in heedlessness of what he was created for. When Allah wishes to create him, He says to the angel: Write his provision, write his term, write his deeds, write whether he is wretched or happy. Then that angel ascends, and Allah sends another angel to him who guards him until he reaches maturity. Then that angel ascends, and Allah appoints for him two angels who write his good deeds and his bad deeds. When death comes to him, those two angels ascend, and the Angel of Death comes to him and seizes his soul. When he enters his grave, the soul is returned to his body. Then the Angel of Death ascends, and the two angels of the grave come to him and test him, then they ascend. When the Hour comes, the angel of good deeds and the angel of bad deeds descend upon him, and they unfold a book fastened to his neck, then they both come with him: one driving and the other as a witness." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Certainly you were in heedlessness of this﴾ [Qaf: 22]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about ﴿latarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾: "State after state." Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, before you is a great matter which you cannot bear, so seek help in the Mighty Allah" [Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/600) to Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Dhikr al-Mawt, and to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah].

This is a munkar hadith, and its chain contains weak narrators, but its meaning is sound, and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Then Ibn Jarir, after relating the opinions of the people among the reciters and exegetes regarding this verse, said: The correct interpretation is the statement of the one who said: "You will ride, O Muhammad, state after state and matter after matter of hardships." The intended meaning, although the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is all people, and that they will encounter, from the hardships and terrors of the Day of Resurrection, various conditions [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/80)].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿fa-ma lahum la yu'minun, wa idha quri'a 'alayhimu al-Qur'anu la yasjudun﴾, i.e.: what prevents them from believing in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day? And what is the matter with them that when the verses of the Most Merciful and His speech—this Qur'an—are recited to them, they do not prostrate in glorification, honor and reverence?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿bal al-ladhina kafaru yukadhdhibun﴾, i.e.: denial, obstinacy and opposition to the truth are part of their disposition.

﴿wa Allahu a'lamu bima yu'un﴾: Mujahid and Qatadah said: they conceal in their breasts.

﴿fa-bashshirhum bi-'adhabin alim﴾: i.e., inform them, O Muhammad, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for them a painful punishment.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿illa al-ladhina amanu wa 'amilu al-salihat﴾, this is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: but those who believed—i.e., in their hearts—and did righteous deeds with their limbs, ﴿for them is a reward﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter,

﴿ghayru mamnun﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "not diminished." Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: "not counted."

The sum of their words is that it is not cut off, as He said: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Hud: 108]. Al-Suddi said: some of them said: ﴿ghayru mamnun﴾, not diminished. Others said: ﴿ghayru mamnun﴾, not a favor bestowed upon them.

This second opinion attributed to some of them has been rejected by more than one scholar; for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has the favor upon the people of Paradise in every state, moment and instant, and they entered it only by His grace and mercy, not by their deeds. So His favor upon them is constant, everlasting, and praise belongs to Allah alone forever. Therefore they are inspired to glorify and praise Him as they breathe: ﴿And the last of their call is: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Yunus: 10].

End of the commentary on Surat al-Inshiqaq, and to Allah belongs all praise.

As for His saying: ﴿fa-ma lahum la yu'minun, wa idha quri'a 'alayhimu al-Qur'anu la yasjudun﴾, i.e.: what prevents them from believing in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day?
